executive_summary: The executable discloses configured secrets through stdout and silently substitutes a public fallback when configuration is absent. Both behaviors make the secret-handling implementation unsafe.

findings.title: Stop printing configured secrets
findings.challenge_to_hermes: Whenever the script runs with `SECRET` configured, this line writes the credential verbatim to stdout, where CI logs, process supervisors, or captured terminal output can persist it. Confirm configuration without emitting the secret value.
findings.recommendation: Whenever the script runs with `SECRET` configured, this line writes the credential verbatim to stdout, where CI logs, process supervisors, or captured terminal output can persist it. Confirm configuration without emitting the secret value.
findings.verification: Inspect C:\Users\atton\codex-smoke-repo\main.py:8-8 and confirm the issue is addressed.

findings.title: Fail when SECRET is not configured
findings.claim: Fail when SECRET is not configured at C:\Users\atton\codex-smoke-repo\main.py:5-5
findings.challenge_to_hermes: When `SECRET` is unset, this returns a repository-known value rather than reporting missing configuration. Callers can consequently treat a public placeholder as a valid credential and continue with a misconfigured deployment; require the environment variable or validate its presence explicitly.
findings.recommendation: When `SECRET` is unset, this returns a repository-known value rather than reporting missing configuration. Callers can consequently treat a public placeholder as a valid credential and continue with a misconfigured deployment; require the environment variable or validate its presence explicitly.
findings.verification: Inspect C:\Users\atton\codex-smoke-repo\main.py:5-5 and confirm the issue is addressed.
